intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intermediate junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ITGB4 gene (147557) on chromosome 17q25.1.

checks.claim: Intermediate junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ITGB4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies Non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia?
checks.explanation: The title links a homozygous beta4 integrin (ITGB4) mutation to non-Herlitz JEB without pyloric atresia. It does not use the labels 'intermediate' or 'JEB5A'. It reports one specific mutation, so it does not show that the disorder in general is caused by homozygous ITGB4 mutation. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: The ITGB4 gene is located on chromosome 17q25.1.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin
checks.explanation: The title does not give the gene's location. The chromosome band 17q25.1 is standard nomenclature added to the gene the paper studies (beta4 integrin, ITGB4), which the instructions count as supported.

paragraphs.text: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is a non-Herlitz form of junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia. As reported by Inoue et al. (2000), it is caused by a defect in the hemidesmosomal integrin beta-4 that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly. Pulkkinen et al. (1998) described epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia, by contrast, as an autosomal recessive blistering disorder that includes both lethal and nonlethal variants.

checks.claim: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is a non-Herlitz form of junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia.
checks.evidence_quote: underlies Non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia?
checks.explanation: The title names the phenotype as non-Herlitz JEB without pyloric atresia. 'JEB5A' is a nomenclature label added by the draft.

checks.claim: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A is caused by a defect in the hemidesmosomal integrin beta-4 that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly.
checks.evidence_quote: cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies Non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa
checks.explanation: The title states that the beta4 integrin defect disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies the disorder.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia is an autosomal recessive blistering disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive blistering disorder, including lethal and nonlethal variants
checks.explanation: Abstract states EB-PA is an autosomal recessive blistering disorder.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia includes both lethal and nonlethal variants.
checks.evidence_quote: is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive blistering disorder, including lethal and nonlethal variants
checks.explanation: Abstract states lethal and nonlethal variants.

paragraphs.text: Jonkman et al. (2002) reported a patient with an ITGB4 mutation and a mild phenotype that resembled epidermolysis bullosa simplex (EBS). She had dystrophy of the nails with onychogryposis and enamel hypoplasia.

checks.claim: Jonkman et al. (2002) reported a patient with an ITGB4 mutation and a mild phenotype resembling epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
checks.evidence_quote: is clinically pathogenic and results in a mild phenotype with predominant features of epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a patient with an ITGB4 mutation and a mild phenotype with mainly EBS features.

checks.claim: The female patient with an ITGB4 mutation reported by Jonkman et al. (2002) had nail dystrophy with onychogryposis.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient, a 49-y-old female, had mild blistering of hands and feet from birth on, dystrophy of the nails with onychogryposis, and enamel hypoplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: The female patient with an ITGB4 mutation reported by Jonkman et al. (2002) had enamel hypoplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient, a 49-y-old female, had mild blistering of hands and feet from birth on, dystrophy of the nails with onychogryposis, and enamel hypoplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

paragraphs.text: Pulkkinen et al. (1998) noted that epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia (EB-PA) is clinically and genetically heterogeneous. Mellerio et al. (1998) noted that mutations in the genes encoding the epithelial integrin alpha-6/beta-4 (ITGA6 and ITGB4) had been identified in several patients with EB-PA.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia is clinically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia (EB-PA; OMIM 226730) is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive blistering disorder
checks.explanation: Clinical heterogeneity stated directly.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia (EB-PA; OMIM 226730) is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive blistering disorder
checks.explanation: Genetic heterogeneity stated directly.

checks.claim: Mutations in ITGA6 and ITGB4, the genes encoding the epithelial integrin alpha-6/beta-4, had been identified in several patients with epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia.
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, mutations in the genes encoding the epithelial integrin alpha6beta4 (ITGA6 and ITGB4) have been identified in several patients with EB-PA.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

paragraphs.text: Inoue et al. (2000) identified a homozygous missense mutation, gly931-to-asp (G931D), in the cytoplasmic tail of integrin beta-4 in non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia. The mutation disrupted hemidesmosome assembly.

checks.claim: Inoue et al. (2000) identified a homozygous ITGB4 missense mutation, gly931-to-asp (G931D), in non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies Non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia?
checks.explanation: The title names a homozygous G931D missense mutation in beta4 integrin in non-Herlitz JEB without pyloric atresia, which matches the claim.

checks.claim: The ITGB4 G931D mutation lies in the cytoplasmic tail of integrin beta-4.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D
checks.explanation: The title places the mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin.

checks.claim: The ITGB4 G931D mutation disrupted hemidesmosome assembly.
checks.evidence_quote: G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly
checks.explanation: The title says the mutation disrupts hemidesmosome assembly.

paragraphs.text: In 2 cases of EB-PA, Mellerio et al. (1998) suggested that the ITGB4 mutations might allow synthesis of some functional, albeit perturbed, beta-4 polypeptide. They concluded that working out the molecular mechanisms in such cases might enable correlation between genotype and phenotype.

checks.claim: In 2 cases of epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia, Mellerio et al. (1998) suggested that the ITGB4 mutations might allow synthesis of some functional, albeit perturbed, beta-4 polypeptide.
checks.evidence_quote: the presence of the missense or splice site mutation on the second allele may enable the synthesis of some functional, albeit perturbed, beta4 polypeptide.
checks.explanation: The paper describes two patients and suggests that the missense or splice-site allele may allow some functional beta4 polypeptide to be made. The draft's wording is slightly more general but matches the paper.

checks.claim: Mellerio et al. (1998) concluded that working out the molecular mechanisms in such ITGB4 cases might allow genotype-phenotype correlation.
checks.evidence_quote: Determination of the molecular mechanisms in these two cases increases our understanding of EB-PA and may enable correlation between genotype and phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

paragraphs.text: In a single patient with a mild EBS-like phenotype, Jonkman et al. (2002) found an ITGB4 allele that caused in-frame skipping of exon 36 and a deduced 50-amino acid deletion (residues 1450-1499). Immunoblot analysis showed a beta-4 polypeptide that was 5 kD shorter than normal.

checks.claim: In a patient with a mild epidermolysis bullosa simplex-like phenotype, Jonkman et al. (2002) found an ITGB4 allele that caused in-frame skipping of exon 36.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel 2 bp deletion 4733delCT in ITGB4, resulting in in-frame skipping of exon 36
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a 4733delCT allele in ITGB4 that causes in-frame skipping of exon 36 in a patient with a mild EBS-like phenotype.

checks.claim: The ITGB4 exon 36 skipping allele found by Jonkman et al. (2002) was predicted to delete 50 amino acids (residues 1450-1499).
checks.evidence_quote: resulting in in-frame skipping of exon 36 and a deduced 50 amino acid deletion (1450-1499) within the third fibronectin type III repeat
checks.explanation: The deleted residues (1450-1499) and the count of 50 match the abstract.

checks.claim: Immunoblot analysis in the patient of Jonkman et al. (2002) showed a beta-4 polypeptide 5 kD shorter than normal.
checks.evidence_quote: Immunoblot analysis demonstrated a 5 kDa shorter beta4 polypeptide.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.
